title: Book: The Richest Man in Babylon — George S. Clason (1926)
publisher: Artha Kavach original summary of a book's ideas (paraphrase, not a quotation; the author's opinion, not settled fact) — pending manual verification
text: George Clason's short parables, set in ancient Babylon, teach timeless money habits. The core rule is 'pay yourself first': set aside at least a tenth of everything you earn before spending on anything else, and treat it as untouchable. The 'cures for a lean purse' add: control your expenses so needs don't swallow your income, make your savings earn more money, guard your capital from loss by seeking advice from experienced people and avoiding get-rich schemes, own your home if it makes sense, provide for future income and family, and keep increasing your ability to earn through skills. It is easy to read and a good first book. Limits: the parables are old, give no modern product guidance, and the 'advice from the wise' idea should not be confused with trusting salespeople.
